scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The hearing
scenes.caption: The festival team presents its security plan. Three priorities need attention: a public registration folder, a possible gate-laptop failure and a stolen password. The team has six exercise tokens to spend on controls.
scenes.dialogue: Can we justify every control we choose?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The budget
scenes.caption: Named access, a tested separate backup and protected individual accounts each cost two tokens. A poster redesign also costs two. A good design spends the available budget on the stated risks rather than unrelated improvements.
scenes.dialogue: A useful change must address the actual failure mode.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Match the control
scenes.caption: Access restrictions reduce unwanted exposure. Recoverable backups support continuity after a failure. Stronger sign-in and private recovery protect accounts. Each control has a purpose, and none can remove every remaining risk.
scenes.dialogue: A backup cannot close an open sharing link.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Your decision
scenes.caption: The registration folder is open through a public link. Choose the control that directly reduces this exposure. Consider what the control changes rather than whether its name sounds secure.
scenes.dialogue: Which choice changes who can reach the data?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: New evidence
scenes.caption: The gate laptop is lost while an organiser session remains active. M F A does not automatically close that session. The team needs to revoke access, assess exposure with the teacher and test its separate backup.
scenes.dialogue: Our plan needs a response to this new event.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the lab
scenes.caption: Defend the plan with its budget, evidence and limitations. Explain a remaining risk and revise after a changed case. In the lab, complete the design review that brings together the whole Cybersecurity module.
scenes.dialogue: A defensible design includes the risks it cannot eliminate.
